implementationAnalyses.conciseReason: The Content Agent document (finalAuthoringContract) explicitly authors a 'Hero Video' block (canonicalBlockName: hero-video, selector: div.herovideo) with a four-cell single-row table structure. The block is a new addition to the repository — no blocks/hero-video directory exists in the repository inventory. The authored table has one row with four cells: [video asset], [heading text], [primary CTA link], [secondary CTA link]. Section metadata (style: full-width, video-container; subtitles; poster; transcript) is authored separately in the section-metadata block and must be preserved as-is per policy preservePageAndSectionMetadataBehavior. The block must render: (1) a configurable video element driven by the authored video asset cell, (2) the playback helper text 'Press Enter or Space to play or pause the video.' as a visually-present but screen-reader-accessible caption, (3) the heading 'DISNEY IMAGINATION CAMPUS - STUDENT TRAVEL REIMAGINED', and (4) two CTA links with labels 'PLAY FULL VIDEO' and 'LEARN MORE'. The live page evidence confirms the block occupies a full-width 1440×630px container (position: relative) with an absolutely-positioned .video-information overlay (x:216, y:373, w:1008, h:205) containing the heading and CTAs in white text (rgb(255,255,255)) centered over the video. The PLAY FULL VIDEO link carries aria-label 'PLAY FULL VIDEO about DISNEY IMAGINATION CAMPUS - STUDENT TRAVEL REIMAGINED' and href '#fullscreen-cta'; LEARN MORE carries aria-label 'LEARN MORE about DISNEY IMAGINATION CAMPUS - STUDENT TRAVEL REIMAGINED' and href '/about'. Both links use font-weight 900 at 24px. The video element must support keyboard play/pause via Enter or Space per the acceptance criteria and the captured helper text. Exact typography, color values, pixel spacing, hover/animation behavior, video source, poster, transcript, and duration are uncaptured and must remain configurable — not hardcoded. The section-metadata block (subtitles, poster, transcript, style) is already authored and will be processed by the EDS section-metadata pipeline; the block JS must read these values from the section's dataset or from the section-metadata rows to configure the video element at runtime. The repository uses standard EDS boilerplate (aem.js, scripts.js) with no existing hero-video block, so two new files are required: blocks/hero-video/hero-video.js and blocks/hero-video/hero-video.css.

requirementTraceability.description: The block renders the captured text content exactly: Video, Press Enter or Space to play or pause the video., and DISNEY IMAGINATION CAMPUS - STUDENT TRAVEL REIMAGINED.
The block includes one configurable video media area and does not hardcode unavailable video source, poster, duration, transcript, spacing, typography, color, hover, or animation values.
The block renders exactly two primary interactive controls using the captured labels PLAY FULL VIDEO and LEARN MORE.
The content sequence follows the captured flow of video affordance, playback helper text, heading, and calls to action.
The call-to-action destinations are configurable because destination URLs were not included in the supplied evidence.
The video interaction supports keyboard operation using Enter or Space, matching the captured playback instruction.
Both calls to action expose clear accessible names matching their visible labels: PLAY FULL VIDEO and LEARN MORE.

implementationAnalyses.conciseReason: The Content Agent document (finalAuthoringContract) contains a grounded block entry for 'Cards (overlay)' with canonicalBlockName 'cards' and selector 'div.cards.overlay'. The authored table has two captured rows — PERFORMING ARTS and ARTS & HUMANITIES — each with three cells: [image-cell][label-cell][link-cell]. The live source text confirms all four category labels (PERFORMING ARTS, ARTS & HUMANITIES, SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY, LEADERSHIP & INNOVATION) and their destination URLs (https://main--disneycampus--twdc-minnie.aem.live/programs/performing-arts and https://main--disneycampus--twdc-minnie.aem.live/programs/arts-humanities are captured; the other two are structurally identical and configurable). The block renders as a <ul> grid absolutely positioned at the bottom of the hero-video section, overlapping it (hence 'overlay' variant). The repository already has blocks/cards/cards.js and blocks/cards/cards.css (boilerplate implementation). This story requires adding an 'overlay' variant to the existing cards block — a new CSS variant class — plus a minimal JS extension to handle the overlay positioning and the label-only (no image body) card structure. No new block folder is created; the variant is added to the existing cards block files. The four items are interactive links (keyboard reachable, accessible name = visible label text including & characters). Destination URLs are configurable via authored link cells. No media, buttons, or descriptive copy are introduced beyond what the Content Agent document captures.

requirementTraceability.description: Render exactly four category items using the captured labels: PERFORMING ARTS, ARTS & HUMANITIES, SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY, and LEADERSHIP & INNOVATION.
Expose each captured category item as an interactive link-like item with its destination configurable because captured link targets were not provided.
Preserve the captured content order of the four category labels.
Do not introduce additional category labels, media, buttons, descriptive copy, or external data behavior not present in the provided evidence.
Each category item must be keyboard reachable and activate through standard keyboard interaction.
Each interactive item must expose an accessible name matching its visible category label, including correct handling of ampersands in ARTS & HUMANITIES and SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY.

visualSummary.layout: The overlay cards sit in a 4-column CSS grid (grid-template-columns: 267.5px × 4, gap: 20px) absolutely positioned at the bottom of the hero-video section. The section has padding-bottom: 200px which creates the visual overlap zone. The <ul> is 1130px wide, centered (x: 155px on a 1440px viewport). Each tile is approximately 267.5px × 267.5px square.
visualSummary.typography: Category labels are uppercase text. The live heading samples show InspireTWDCBlack / Arial, font-weight 900, letter-spacing 3px at 28px for similar headings. The overlay tiles use the same heavy weight treatment. Text is white (rgb(255,255,255)) on a dark/semi-transparent tile background.
visualSummary.interactivity: Each tile is an interactive link. The live source text confirms anchor hrefs (e.g. /programs/performing-arts). Keyboard focus must be reachable via Tab; Enter/Space activates. Focus style should use a visible outline consistent with the project's existing focus patterns.
visualSummary.responsive: Desktop: 4-column grid, 267.5px columns. Tablet/mobile: grid must reflow — 2 columns at medium breakpoints, 1 column at small. The absolute positioning within the hero section must be reconsidered at mobile (likely static flow or adjusted bottom offset).
visualSummary.colors: Tile background: captured page colors include rgb(207,16,45) (Disney red) and dark overlays. The exact tile background is not captured in computed styles for the overlay cards specifically; it is expressed as a CSS custom property to remain configurable.
visualSummary.ampersandHandling: The HTML source uses & for & in 'ARTS & HUMANITIES' and 'SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY'. The authored link text and aria-label must decode to the literal & character so screen readers announce the correct name.

implementationAnalyses.conciseReason: The story requires a reusable header block that renders the captured contact content (Questions?, Call (321) 939 7560, Contact Us) and primary navigation labels (ABOUT US, CURRICULUM & TICKETS, SPECIAL EVENTS, PLAN YOUR TRIP, CONNECT WITH US) with configurable link destinations. The repository already contains blocks/header/header.js and blocks/header/header.css at the expected paths. The existing header.js follows the canonical EDS pattern: it loads a /nav fragment document, reads three sections (brand, sections, tools) from that fragment, and decorates them into a nav element with hamburger, brand, nav-sections, and nav-tools areas. The existing header.css provides the full nav layout including hamburger, brand, sections, and tools grid areas with responsive behaviour. The Content Agent document does NOT include a header block table — the header is a global shared component loaded via fragment convention (/nav document), not an inline page block. This is confirmed by: (1) scripts.js calls loadHeader(doc.querySelector('body > header')) in loadLazy, (2) header.js uses loadFragment(navPath) where navPath defaults to '/nav', (3) the repository inventory shows fragmentSupport.conventions.navigation = '/nav'. Therefore the header is NOT a content-gap block requiring a new table structure — it is a GLOBAL fragment-driven pattern. The implementation work is: modify blocks/header/header.js to support a contact bar row (row index 0 of the /nav fragment) containing the Questions? prompt, phone number, and Contact Us link, in addition to the existing brand/sections/tools rows; modify blocks/header/header.css to style the contact bar and nav-sections bar to match the captured evidence (contact bar above brand/nav, nav-sections bar with black background at y:131, height:50px, flex justify-content:center); and update styles/styles.css --nav-height to reflect the observed two-row header height (~160px desktop). The captured evidence shows: header-wrapper rect height 160px, nav element height 181px, nav-sections div at y:131 height:50px with background-color rgb(0,0,0) and justify-content:center, nav ul (menubar) max-width:1080px with justify-content:space-between. The contact bar content (Questions?, Call (321) 939 7560, Contact Us) is observed in the header region text. The logo/brand and search control are referenced in acceptance criteria as 'where available from rendered evidence' — the brand area is already handled by the existing nav-brand section; a search control is not present in the captured computed-style evidence for the header region and must be flagged as a content gap. The /nav fragment document must be authored by the Content Agent with four sections: (0) contact bar, (1) brand/logo, (2) nav sections list, (3) tools/search — but since the Content Agent document does not include this fragment, it is flagged as a content gap. The JS and CSS changes are scoped entirely to blocks/header/ and a --nav-height token update in styles/styles.css.

requirementTraceability.description: The header renders the captured contact content exactly as observed: Questions?, Call (321) 939 7560, and Contact Us.
The primary navigation renders the captured labels exactly as observed: ABOUT US, CURRICULUM & TICKETS, SPECIAL EVENTS, PLAN YOUR TRIP, and CONNECT WITH US.
The block supports configurable link destinations for Contact Us and each primary navigation item because most destination URLs were not captured.
The block supports the observed Disney Imagination Campus logo/link and search control from rendered evidence without requiring uncaptured styling or behavior assumptions.
The implementation does not hardcode uncaptured typography, spacing, colors, hover states, motion, or link destinations.
The header is exposed as a page header landmark and all interactive header items are reachable by keyboard in a logical order.
All interactive controls and links have accessible names matching or clearly representing their visible labels, including Contact Us and the primary navigation labels.
